# Winter tyres

## Why bother in Bristol

Most years we get maybe 3 days of snow. But I'm out at 6am to jobs up in the Mendips and the Chew Valley, and the lanes past Compton Martin don't get gritted. After sliding gently into a verge near Blagdon in Jan 2023 (no damage, just pride) I decided to do a proper set. Rule of thumb from the tyre fitter: winter compound grips better than summer tyres once it's under 7°C, and in a Bristol winter that's most mornings from November.

## What I bought

- 4x Nokian WR Snowproof 205/55 R16 91H
- On 4 secondhand steel wheels off eBay, 16x6.5 ET39, £90 the lot from a bloke in Yate (seller "astrabits_yate"). Saves paying for fitting twice a year
- Fitted and balanced at Hartcliffe Tyre Co, invoice HTC-7781, £412 tyres plus £40 fitting
- 3PMSF symbol on the sidewall, the snowflake on a mountain. M+S alone means nothing

## Swap dates

- On: 18 Nov 2023 at 108,950 miles
- Off: 23 Mar 2024 at 111,600
- On: 9 Nov 2024 at 116,220
- Off: 29 Mar 2025 at 119,700

Summer set lives in the shed in tyre bags, stacked flat, not standing on the tread.

## Wear and notes for next time

- Tread at the end of the 2nd season: 6.1mm fronts, 6.8mm rears. Winters lose a lot of grip under about 4mm, so swap fronts to rears at the next fit
- Check the pressures after every swap, the steel wheel set has the old valves and loses a bit. Numbers in [[Tyre pressure]]
- Insurer said winters aren't a modification but I had to ring and ask, see [[Car insurance renewal]]
- Would have wanted studs for [[Iceland ring road]]
- The whole set went with the car in the end, see [[Selling the old hatchback]]
